summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators have become the dominant way corporations consume foundation models in 2026, offering managed access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere and others inside the customer's own cloud security perimeter. These platforms differ not in whether they are enterprise-grade (most are) but in model selection, data-residency guarantees, pricing units, and how well they fit an organization's existing cloud contracts. The market is led by the three hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google), with data-platform-native options (Snowflake, Databricks) and enterprise-governance plays (IBM watsonx, Oracle) carving out specialized niches.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and completions stay within the company's own VPC/cloud tenant and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying legal and IP concerns.
Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the hyperscaler's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP and GDPR/EU data-boundary guarantees, which raw vendor APIs often cannot match.
Single billing and procurement: model usage rolls into an existing cloud contract or committed-spend agreement, avoiding net-new vendor onboarding, security review, and separate invoices.
Unified identity, networking and governance: IAM/Entra integration, PrivateLink/private endpoints, centralized audit logging, and key management reuse the enterprise's existing controls.

Model optionality and portability: a single managed API exposes many competing models (Claude, GPT, Llama, Gemini, Mistral) so teams can switch or route between models without re-architecting integrations.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens by model, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; discounts via Azure committed spend (MACC).
key_features: Content filtering and responsible AI controls
Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-centric enterprises needing the earliest access to OpenAI frontier models with deep Entra/Office 365 integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing per model, Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity, and Batch inference discounts; billed through AWS account.
key_features: Guardrails for content and PII filtering
platforms.best_for: AWS-native enterprises wanting the widest multi-vendor model choice (especially Claude) under existing IAM and VPC controls.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token / per-character by model, plus Provisioned Throughput measured in GSUs (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec); committed-use discounts available.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and private access
Grounding with Google Search and enterprise data
Data not used to train models
platforms.best_for: Data-and-analytics-heavy organizations on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus multi-vendor models with strong grounding/RAG.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumed in Snowflake credits based on tokens processed; folds into existing Snowflake consumption contract.
key_features: Models run next to governed data in Snowflake
No data movement out of the warehouse
platforms.best_for: Enterprises that want to run LLMs directly against governed data already in Snowflake without building a separate AI stack.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for Foundation Model APIs and DBU-based pricing for provisioned throughput; part of Databricks consumption contract.
key_features: Unity Catalog governance over models and data
Mosaic AI Gateway for rate limiting/routing
platforms.best_for: Data-engineering and ML teams building custom and fine-tuned models on the lakehouse with strong governance.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource-unit (RU) / token-based pricing; available as SaaS or on-prem/hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data; subscription and consumption options.
key_features: watsonx Orchestrate for enterprise AI agents
platforms.best_for: Highly regulated industries (finance, government, healthcare) needing on-prem/hybrid deployment, governance, and IP indemnification.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrates with OCI Universal Credits.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated capacity
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and Fusion Applications customers wanting generative AI integrated with ERP/HCM data in their OCI tenancy.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: Various open embedding and image models
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go priced in 'Neurons' (compute units) per model with a free allocation tier; no long-term commitment required.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and routing
Vectorize vector database and R2 integration
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, serverless edge inference with open models close to end users.

platforms.name: Together AI / Fireworks AI (managed open-model APIs)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token by model plus dedicated/reserved GPU endpoints; volume discounts and private deployment options.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardizing on open-weight models that want optimized price-performance and the option of private deployment.
